response.sql: WITH matched AS (SELECT o.mktnote AS pair, f.feerate - f.rebrate AS net FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON o.recordvault = f.orderslink), pair_avg AS (SELECT pair, AVG(net) AS avg_net FROM matched GROUP BY pair), bench AS (SELECT AVG(avg_net) AS b FROM pair_avg), kept AS (SELECT p.avg_net, p.avg_net - b.b AS excess FROM pair_avg p CROSS JOIN bench b WHERE p.avg_net > b.b) SELECT AVG(avg_net) AS avg_of_avg_net_fee_rate, AVG(excess) AS avg_excess_over_benchmark FROM kept

assumptions.assumption: Records with NULL mktnote form a single group, which GROUP BY does naturally. That group's average counts as one pair in the benchmark.

A NULL feerate or rebrate makes that record's net rate NULL, so AVG skips it. A pair whose records are all NULL has a NULL average. That pair still counts as a group but is skipped in the benchmark average and never passes the > comparison.
If no pair exceeds the benchmark, the single output row has NULLs.
